Script Draft - Verbatim

The script is the source - these words do not change in production

Speaker is Aelune throughout, except the student's quoted lines inside the Story. She demonstrates before she explains. Pauses after punch lines are part of the script - see the standards mapping.

Hook

"I'll try" is sometimes a promise - and sometimes an exit you built before you entered.

Story - the list of tries

A student came to my shelf carrying a list. Not a list of things done. A list of things she would try. She would try the new work. She would try the new habit. She would try to mend the friendship. She would try to rest, try to begin, try to be brave. Twelve tries, all earnest, all unfinished, all still waiting at the door.

I did not lecture her. I set out two bowls and a vessel of clear water. Into the first bowl I poured half, and stopped. We waited. The water stayed cloudy, unsettled, catching the lamplight in a troubled way. Into the second bowl I poured fully, to the brim, and waited again. It cleared. It held the light steady.

Delivery note. The demonstration comes before any explanation. Let both waits play in real time - the cloudiness and the clearing are the teaching, before a word of it is spoken.
First in Consciousness - Speech 5 Production PackagePage 2
Script Draft - Verbatim, Continued

The half bowl, and the third door

"The half bowl is not modest," I said. "It is undecided. And undecided water cannot carry anything."

She looked at the two bowls a long time. Then she said the truest thing of the evening: "'I'll try' lets me quit without ever saying no, and fail without ever having said yes."

She was afraid of both - afraid of the yes, because it would bind her, and afraid of the no, because it would close a door. So she had built herself a third door, a door that was not a door at all, and she had been standing in its frame for a year.

Delivery notes for this section.
Hold a pause after "undecided water cannot carry anything."
The student's confession is quoted, not paraphrased - it is the turn of the story.
"A door that was not a door at all" lands quietly, then stillness, before the reframe.
First in Consciousness - Speech 5 Production PackagePage 3
Script Draft - Verbatim, Continued

Step in fully, or sit on the bank honestly

Reframe

Hear me. Step in fully, or sit on the bank honestly. Both are respectable. The half-step is the only dishonest position. Commitment is not pressure. Commitment is honesty. A clear no is kinder than a cloudy yes - kinder to you, kinder to everyone waiting on your answer.

The Current cannot carry half of you. It carries what is wholly in it, and it leaves the rest on the bank, not out of cruelty, but out of nature: a river cannot carry a foot that has not left the shore.

Do not confuse the half-step with humility. Humility says, "I cannot do this, and I will say so." The half-step says nothing, and promises everything, and delivers the cloud.

Delivery note. "Step in fully, or sit on the bank honestly" is the aphorism of the episode - it also carries the Short. Hold a full pause after it, and after "The Current cannot carry half of you."
First in Consciousness - Speech 5 Production PackagePage 4
Script Draft - Verbatim, Continued

Retire one "I'll try"

Practice

So this week, pick one thing. One thing from your list of tries. Say it plainly, out loud, witnessed if you can bear it: "I am doing this." Or: "I am not doing this." Retire one "I'll try" - cross it out, say it aloud, let it go. One sentence, spoken, is worth a year of standing in the frame. Do not pick twelve things. Pick one. The Current is wide enough for one whole step. It was never wide enough for twelve halves.

Payoff / Bridge

Clarity is restful. Saying plainly what you will and will not do is the deepest rest I know - deeper than sleep, because sleep does not settle an undecided life. And once you are rested in that clarity, a new question rises, quiet and fair: what deserves your strength at all? Not everything you could carry is yours to carry. That is next week's teaching: small is not a measurement, and strength is not a size.

Where this sits in the episode. End of script draft. The payoff sits at 70-85% of runtime in the scene map, and the bridge - not a hard goodbye - carries the viewer to Speech 6, "Small Is Not a Measurement."
The episode's punch lines, each followed by a full pause: "The half-step is the only dishonest position." "The Current cannot carry half of you." "Clarity is restful."

Crossroads Standards - Mapped to This Episode

The Crossroads standard governs this episode, choice by choice

The standards already set for Crossroads of Identity - the way the video moves, the way it feels, and the way the conversation goes - are the standard for this episode and everything after it. Each standard below is mapped to what it means, concretely, in Speech 5.

Crossroads standardHow Speech 5 maps to it
Pipeline orderFollow the VisionWeaver Studio order with no steps skipped: Avatar Engineering, Worlds & Locations, Books & script, Locks & maps, Cast & avatars, Shot bible, Pictures, Motion, Narration booth, Sound & music, Edit, Deliver, Publish & social. This package completes the script and locks stage.
ContinuityAelune's locked portrait is the single reference for every scene - lavender-grey skin, glowing violet veins, feathery antennae, pale-gold eyes, star-chart shawl. Consistency and hallucination checks on every scene before it passes to edit. The Night Shelf observatory stays one place, at night, all episode; the river in Scene 9 is pictured inside her teaching, never as a second present-day location.
Conversation flowElder mode: the teacher demonstrates before explaining - the two bowls are poured before a word of teaching. Short lines, pauses after punch lines, no lecturing at any point.
VoicesAelune has one distinct cast voice - no impression of any existing character. The student is a second voice, heard in the Story and the confession. Narration is generated in chunks of 30 seconds or less per scene. Captions come from Whisper-class ASR, checked against the script.
Motion and feelVisual change every 8-15 seconds. Hook in under 8 seconds, with no branding opener. Pacing reset every 30-60 seconds. Payoff at 70-85% of runtime. Bridge outro - never a hard goodbye.
SoundMusic sits 9-12 dB under the voice. Soft night ambience runs under the observatory - still air, distant night sounds, the pour of water given its own quiet space in Scenes 4 and 5.
Render and QCGen-4.5 / Act-Two-class workflow, as in the Crossroads pipeline, when funding returns. Budget is measured as cost per finished second. Discipline is preview, verify, publish - nothing publishes from an unverified render.
Status: Writing, images, and files only - no render, no recording, nothing published for this episode.

Description

A student came to Aelune's shelf carrying a list - not of things done, but of things she would try. Twelve tries, all earnest, all unfinished. Aelune did not lecture her. She set out two bowls and a vessel of clear water: the half pour stayed cloudy and unsettled, and the full pour cleared and held the light steady. The half bowl is not modest. It is undecided - and undecided water cannot carry anything.

This week's practice is one thing, not twelve. Pick one thing from your list of tries and say it plainly, out loud: "I am doing this," or "I am not doing this." Retire one "I'll try." The Current is wide enough for one whole step. It was never wide enough for twelve halves.
